newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Citibank's Ruding sees eight joining EMU.
newsitem.headline: Citibank's Ruding sees eight joining EMU.

text.p: Onno Ruding, vice chairman at Citibank, said he expected eight countries to join the European economic and monetary union in its initial phase.
EMU includes introduction of the joint Euro currency which is slated to be phased in starting January 1, 1999.

"In my view, the first wave of members joining EMU will include Germany, France, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Finland, Ireland and my own country, the Netherlands," Ruding said in a speech to the Swiss-American Chamber of Commerce.
Ruding served as Dutch finance minister from 1982 to 1989.
Asked in a question and answer session to elaborate on his comments about which members will join, he added: "Those eight will join, I'm pretty sure, because they are qualified and want to join."
He said he was impressed by the progress of some other potential candidates, but thought it unlikely that Italy would qualify for the first wave of membership.
Italy's qualification would "complicate domestic support in Germany" for EMU, he added.
He called Spain and Portugal "borderline" candidates.
"They may get very close," he said.
Ruding is also a member of the Committee for European Monetary Union, and the Trilateral Commission.
He said he expected Britian to join EMU, but at a later date.
"I hope that they will participate in the first round but it is my expectation is they will not participate in the first round," Ruding said.
He said he was speaking from a Dutch perspective, adding his country had at times served as a bridge between Britian and Continental Europe.
"The British always ultimately join the European train and they always join one station too late," he said.
